input: Veridamine improves sleep quality by 18% and is clinically proven. Einstein won the Nobel Prize in Physics for the theory of relativity. I love it!

claims.sentence: Veridamine improves sleep quality by 18% and is clinically proven.
claims.rationale: Leans contradicted, but the confidence (0.62) is below the bar to state it. Support: 4 source(s) -> 1 independent line(s) of evidence; strongest: Veridamine supplementation and subjective sleep quality: a pilot randomized trial (randomized controlled trial, n=48, not preregistered, industry-funded). Against: Veridamine for sleep quality in adults: a multicentre preregistered randomized controlled trial (randomized controlled trial, n=612, preregistered, publicly funded): "In a preregistered multicentre randomized controlled trial of 612 adults, veridamine did not significantly improve sleep quality compared with placebo (difference 2%, p = 0.41)."

supporting.title: Veridamine supplementation and subjective sleep quality: a pilot randomized trial
supporting.study: randomized controlled trial, n=48, not preregistered, industry-funded
supporting.text: In a pilot randomized trial of 48 adults, veridamine supplementation improved self-reported sleep quality scores by 18% compared with placebo (p = 0.04).

supporting.title: New supplement boosts sleep quality by 18%, study finds
supporting.text: A new study found that veridamine improves sleep quality by 18%.

supporting.title: Why I take veridamine every night
supporting.text: Science shows veridamine improves sleep quality, so I started taking it.

supporting.title: VeriSleep product page
supporting.text: Clinically proven: veridamine improves sleep quality by 18%.

contradicting.title: Veridamine for sleep quality in adults: a multicentre preregistered randomized controlled trial
contradicting.study: randomized controlled trial, n=612, preregistered, publicly funded
contradicting.text: In a preregistered multicentre randomized controlled trial of 612 adults, veridamine did not significantly improve sleep quality compared with placebo (difference 2%, p = 0.41).

contradicting.title: Dietary supplements for insomnia: a systematic review
contradicting.text: Current evidence does not support recommending veridamine for improving sleep quality.

red_flags.message: A larger study (randomized controlled trial, n=612, preregistered, publicly funded) did not replicate the original finding.
4 supporting sources trace back to 1 independent study.
Supporting research was funded by a company with a financial interest.
The supporting study has small samples (largest n=48).
